newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico state pension to charge 1.2-1.4 pct fees.
newsitem.headline: Mexico state pension to charge 1.2-1.4 pct fees.

text.p: Mexican workers who do not opt for a private pension fund will be charged between 1.2 and 1.4 percent commission by a central bank "concentrating account," a government source said on Wednesday.

"The percentage to be charged is still under discussion... The commission is estimated at between 1.2 and 1.4 percent," a source from the National Commission for the Retirement Savings System (CONSAR) told Reuters.
The source, who asked not to be named, said a meeting on Friday would fix the final level of commission.

More than 10 million Mexican workers will be able to choose as of July 1 from 18 competing private pension funds, or Afores, in which to deposit retirement savings accounts currently held by the state-run Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS).
The Afores will administer an estimated $5.5 billion per year in pension funds.

The leading center-left candidate in the July 6 race for Mexico City mayor, Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, has criticized the Afores for charging commissions of up to 25 percent, and urged workers to opt instead for the central bank account.
